[1] Distributionally-Verifiable Rewards for Human-Behavior Simulation cs.CL | cs.AI | cs.LGPDF

Ruoyun Ma, Shuang Liu, Peiye Liu, Ao Qu, Baichuan Mo

TL;DR: 论文提出 Distributionally-Verifiable Rewards（DVR），一种用于 LLM 模拟人类调查回答的强化学习奖励，通过在每个问题-人口统计群体边际内对齐模型生成频率与人类回答频率，引导个体回答并保持群体分布。方法在 OpinionQA 上评估，在保持逐回答准确率的同时显著降低 JSD，并提升人口统计结构相关指标。

Details

Motivation: 现有 LLM 调查模拟训练难以同时兼顾个体回答预测、总体分布匹配和人口统计差异刻画：精确匹配奖励会偏向高频回答，而聚合分布匹配可能忽略人口统计信息仍然取得较低分布误差。

Result: 在 OpinionQA 数据集上，与仅优化准确率的 RLVR 相比，DVR 保持逐回答准确率，并将 JSD 在分布内降低 34.5%、在留出问题上降低 14.6%，两个划分上的 DPC 点估计也更高；对比 KL-SFT 与忽略人口统计的边际匹配表明，低 JSD 不足以证明对群体异质性的忠实性。

Insight: 创新点在于将人口统计群体分布差距引入可验证奖励，并以问题-群体边际内的生成频率与人类回答频率对齐来指导个体级回答，而非仅优化精确匹配或总体分布。客观上看，其价值在于把准确率、分布拟合和人口统计结构纳入统一评估与训练信号，强调三者需共同评价。

Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to simulate survey respondents in social-science research. A useful simulator should predict individual responses, reproduce population response distributions, and capture demographic differences. Common training approaches struggle to balance these goals: exact-match rewards encourage the model to concentrate on the most frequent human response, which is contradictory to the goal of distributional alignment. Meanwhile, aggregate distribution matching can look good even when demographic information is ignored. To this end, we introduce Distributionally-Verifiable Rewards (DVR), a reinforcement-learning reward that uses demographic group distribution gaps to guide individual responses, designed by aligning policy generated frequencies with human response frequencies within each question-group margins. We evaluate the method using the OpinionQA dataset and find that comparing with accuracy-only RLVR, DVR preserves per-response accuracy while reducing JSD by 34.5% in-distribution and 14.6% on held-out questions, with higher DPC point estimates on both splits. Comparing KL-SFT with the demographics-blind marginal further shows that low JSD is insufficient to establish fidelity to population heterogeneity, highlighting that accuracy, distributional fit, and demographic structure should be evaluated together.

[2] Benchmarking and Adapting LLMs for English-Swedish Medical Question Answering cs.CL | cs.AIPDF

Seyed Alireza Molavi, Zhan Su, Stefan Byttner, Yan Hu, Peyman Sheikholharam Mashhadi

TL;DR: 论文面向英语-瑞典语医疗问答，构建了一个条目对齐的英瑞双语基准，并提出用翻译训练数据与开放教师模型生成的推理轨迹来适配小模型。实验表明小模型在瑞典语下性能下降更明显，而加入瑞典语推理轨迹微调可显著缩小差距，使1.2B学生模型在瑞典语上从23.5%提升到52.0%。

Details

Motivation: 现有LLM在英语医疗考试上表现较好，但其瑞典语医疗问答能力尚不清楚，尤其影响医院可本地部署的小型开放模型。论文旨在缩小英语-瑞典语医疗问答差距，并服务于本地化、低资源场景。

Result: 在构建的英瑞医疗多选题基准上，小模型在瑞典语下比大模型损失更多准确率，尤其在无推理作答时。用含瑞典语的推理轨迹微调后，1.2B学生模型瑞典语准确率从23.5%升至52.0%，略高于20B开放模型的快速模式，且内存约为其六分之一。

Insight: 创新点包括：从十个医疗多选题数据集构建保持选项与答案一致的英瑞条目对齐基准；用开放模型发现翻译错误、结合瑞典语医学术语库定位，并由盲评投票决定是否保留编辑；以及利用翻译数据和教师模型推理轨迹对小模型进行英/瑞/双语微调。客观看，其可借鉴之处在于高质量对齐基准构建、保守翻译修复流程和推理轨迹蒸馏对低资源语言适配的有效性。

Abstract: Large language models do well on English medical exams, but less is known about Swedish. This matters most for small open models that hospitals can run locally. To reduce this gap, we first build an item-aligned English-Swedish benchmark from ten medical multiple-choice datasets; each Swedish item keeps the options and answer of its English source. A conservative refinement loop repairs the translations: open models from three families find errors, ground them in a Swedish medical term base, and keep a model-written edit only if blind judges vote for it. On this benchmark, small models lose much more accuracy in Swedish than large ones, especially when they answer without reasoning. Second, we ask whether English data and open teacher models can close this gap. We translate the training data, let teachers write reasoning traces, and fine-tune two small students on gold answers or traces in English, Swedish, or both. Training on reasoning traces that include Swedish closes the gap and lifts the 1.2B student from 23.5% to 52.0% in Swedish, slightly above a 20B open model in its fast mode, with a sixth of its memory. We release the benchmark, its edit history, and the code.

[3] Language Model Harnesses can be Compositional Generalizers cs.CL | cs.AIPDF

Alex L. Zhang, Souradip Chakraborty, Omar Khattab

TL;DR: 论文研究神经符号语言模型harness的训练与组合泛化能力。作者提出围绕Recursive Language Model等harness进行强化学习后训练，使其学会程序化地分解复杂任务，从而让每次神经LM调用都处于局部分布内。实验表明，短任务训练可泛化到2-64倍更长的任务，且可跨领域迁移；进一步提出surrogate harness training，用合成代理环境训练RLM-27B，在CTC-Bench和ExpertLongBench等长上下文任务上平均提升26.9%，推理token约减少2倍。

Details

Motivation: 标准LM agent harness会不断累积上下文，迫使神经网络泛化到长程复杂任务，导致长horizon任务训练昂贵且耗时。论文希望训练本身具有神经符号结构的harness，通过程序化外部化管理上下文和组合已有LM能力，以更低计算成本获得组合泛化。

Result: 仅在短任务上训练即可泛化到长2-64倍的任务，优于基础神经LM的提升；在一个领域训练可迁移到共享潜在结构的新领域。用合成数据训练的RLM-27B在CTC-Bench和ExpertLongBench等困难长上下文任务上，相比同一RLM harness中的Qwen3.8-27B平均提升26.9%，推理时token约少2倍。

Insight: 摘要宣称的创新点在于：训练神经符号harness以实现组合泛化，并让harness通过递归子harness调用组合已学分解；提出surrogate harness training，用带假工具/子调用的合成代理环境针对harness内单个LLM调用进行训练。客观来看，其核心创新是把组合泛化从单纯扩大模型能力转向“模型权重+程序化harness结构”的协同训练，为长上下文和长horizon任务提供了可借鉴的降本路径。

Abstract: Modern language models (LMs) are post-trained and deployed as agents inside a “harness”, but standard harness designs accumulate context that the neural network is forced to generalize to, making training for long-horizon tasks expensive and time-consuming. We study an alternative emerging path: training inherently neurosymbolic LM harnesses, which externalize and manage context programmatically to compose existing LM capabilities. We hypothesize that training around these harnesses can offer a better return on compute by enabling compositional generalization, as they can learn to decompose complex problems so that every observation their neural LM receives is locally in-distribution, even when the full task is novel. We find that harnesses like the Recursive Language Model (RLM) learn such decompositions readily under reinforcement learning post-training: (1) we demonstrate that training only on short tasks can generalize to tasks 2-64$\times$ longer while the base neural LM improves less, and (2) training on one domain transfers to novel domains that share latent structure. On messier, complex tasks, we find that we can target individual LLM calls within a harness by generating and training on easier, synthetically generated surrogate environments with fake tool / sub-calls, a technique we call surrogate harness training. From this finding, we train RLM-27B on synthetic data, and show it improves Qwen3.8-27B in the same RLM harness on a hard suite of long-context tasks like CTC-Bench and ExpertLongBench by 26.9% on average while using $\sim$2$\times$ fewer tokens at inference time. Finally, we show that harnesses can compose over these newly learned decompositions using recursive sub-harness calls.

[4] Contrastive On-Policy Distillation via Dual-Branch Supervision cs.CLPDF

Zhibo Hou, Fan Zhao, Yiping Li, Zhiyu An, Wan Du

TL;DR: 论文研究on-policy蒸馏中教师模型的可教性问题，提出对比式on-policy蒸馏cOPD。该方法在学生生成的prefix上同时对比强教师、弱教师和学生三者的预测，形成双分支监督，从而筛选更有利于推理的token候选。实验覆盖数学推理、指令遵循和带弃答的问答任务，并在多种教师-学生配置下验证有效性。

Details

Motivation: 传统OPD倾向于选择能力更强的模型作为教师，但更高任务性能不一定意味着更强的可教性。论文通过受控token干预发现，即使弱于学生的模型也可作为有信息量的对比参考，因此希望利用强弱教师与学生之间的对比信号改进蒸馏。

Result: cOPD在数学推理、指令遵循和带弃答问答三类任务上取得最佳或顶级表现；在数学推理上，整体Pass@16相比最强基线最多提升7.51%。分析还表明该方法能抑制不良响应模式，并可能促进探索。

Insight: 创新点在于将强教师、弱教师和学生预测在学生生成前缀上进行三方对比，用双分支监督选择与更好或更差推理结果相关的token候选。其可取之处是重新审视“教师越强越好”的假设，并把弱模型作为对比参照而非直接模仿目标。

Abstract: For on-policy distillation (OPD), more capable models are a natural choice as teachers. However, higher task performance does not necessarily imply greater teachability. A controlled token intervention study suggests that even a model weaker than the student can serve as an informative contrastive reference. Building on this observation, we propose Contrastive On-Policy Distillation (cOPD), which provides dual branch supervision by contrasting strong teacher, weak teacher, and student predictions at student generated prefixes. Our analysis explains how this three way comparison helps select token candidates associated with better or worse reasoning outcomes under an idealized model. We evaluate cOPD across diverse teacher student configurations spanning different training stages, parameter scales, and model families, on tasks including mathematical reasoning, instruction following, and question answering with abstention. cOPD achieves the best or top-tier performance among the evaluated baselines across all three tasks, improving overall Pass@16 on mathematical reasoning by up to 7.51% over the strongest baseline. Further analyses show that cOPD suppresses undesirable response patterns and suggest that it facilitates exploration.

[5] Language models compress human preference geometry while political structure remains prompt-sensitive cs.CLPDF

Adolfo Ignacio Fuentes-Jofre, Cristian Candia

TL;DR: 论文用智利、法国、巴西成年人的匹配成对政策选择数据，回放测试三个开源权重模型家族，考察LLM能否作为“合成公众”复现个体选择、群体异质性和政治结构。结果显示没有任何提示/设置条件能同时复现三者，最稳定的现象是模型压缩了潜在偏好空间；政治结构虽可被提示改变并更接近人类模式，但群体几何仍被压缩。

Details

Motivation: 已有研究记录了LLM在个体回答错误、群体异质性和提示鲁棒性上的问题，但不清楚这些失败是否反映共同的保真度损失，还是合成公众的不同属性。论文试图在个体、群体和政治结构三个层面系统检验LLM合成公众的保真度。

Result: 在27种智利条件和跨国复制中，没有条件能同时复现个体选择、群体异质性和政治组织；合成参与者方差仅为人参考的0.4%–10.5%，且在全部270次匹配重拟合中均低于人类方差。提示改变会显著影响政治结构：反转提案位置改变12.3%–31.2%的选择，显式标注左右自评量表端点改变20.5%–28.1%的选择，并使提案级左右分裂指标在三国均更接近人类模式；但匹配一致率仅提高3.1–4.2个百分点，参与者几何仍被压缩。

Insight: 摘要宣称的创新点在于将合成公众保真度拆分为个体选择、群体异质性和政治结构三个可分别评估的层面，并通过跨国匹配数据和提示干预区分“政治可读性”与“群体保真度”。客观看，论文较有新意地指出LLM可恢复显著政治分歧却压缩人类偏好多样性，且保真度取决于checkpoint、prompt和setting的组合而非单一模型。

Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to construct synthetic publics. Prior work has documented errors in individual responses, population heterogeneity, and prompt robustness, but whether these failures reflect a common loss of fidelity or distinct properties of synthetic populations remains unclear. We tested this using matched pairwise policy choices from 1,991 Chilean, 843 French, and 434 Brazilian adults replayed through three open-weight model families. Across a 27-condition Chilean grid and cross-country factorial replications, no condition jointly reproduced individual choices, population heterogeneity, and political organization. The most consistent result was compression of the latent preference space: synthetic participant variance was only 0.4-10.5% of the corresponding human reference in the primary comparisons and remained below human variance in all 270 matched refits. Political structure was much more sensitive to how choices were elicited. Reversing proposal position changed 12.3-31.2% of decoded choices. Explicitly labeling the endpoints of the numeric left-right self-placement scale changed 20.5-28.1% of choices and moved an independent proposal-level measure of left-right cleavage toward the human pattern in all three settings. Yet matched agreement improved by only 3.1-4.2 percentage points and participant geometry remained compressed. In Chile, the same intervention compressed the synthetic population further. These results separate political legibility from population fidelity: language models can recover salient political divisions while failing to preserve the breadth of human preference variation. Synthetic-public fidelity is therefore a property of the checkpoint, prompt, and setting, not of a checkpoint alone, and must be evaluated separately at individual, population, and political-structure levels.

[6] Muted Distillation: Sealing Reasoning from Teacher Unlocks Token-Efficient Agents cs.CLPDF

Yuwei Zhang, Ian Miao, Wentao Zhang, Chen Qu, Bill Bi

TL;DR: 论文研究多轮智能体任务中 on-policy distillation（OPD）导致学生模型推理长度增加的问题，提出 Muted Distillation（MD）：在对学生输出进行教师评分时隐藏学生的推理过程，使教师只根据学生行为进行判断。该方法实现简单、无需额外数据或超参数，在知识工作类基准上显著降低输出 token，同时保持或提升任务准确率。

Details

Motivation: 标准 OPD 在多轮智能体任务中会使学生模型训练后推理变长，作者发现推理 token 长度受学生推理对教师评分的干扰程度影响，因此希望减少这种干扰以实现更简洁的智能体推理。

Result: 在 OfficeQA Pro 和 SpreadsheetBench 上，相比标准 OPD，MD 将每轮输出 token 分别降低 57% 和 53%；在 OfficeQA Pro 上准确率与 OPD 相当，在 SpreadsheetBench 上 pass@1 提升 4.8 个百分点。

Insight: 创新点在于对 OPD 做极简修改：教师评分时屏蔽学生推理，只评价学生行为，从而避免学生通过冗长推理“干扰”教师打分。客观上，该方法以很低实现成本缓解了蒸馏中的推理膨胀问题，并兼顾 token 效率与任务表现。

Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) is commonly adopted as one of the components in post-training of large language models (LLMs), but in multi-turn agentic tasks we find that the student model increases their reasoning lengths after training. Our empirical analysis shows that the reasoning token lengths is affected by how much the student can distract the teacher’s scores. We introduce Muted Distillation (MD), a simple variant of OPD that hides the student’s reasoning from the teacher, so the teacher judges what the student does without the interference of student’s reasonings. MD takes a few lines of code and adds no extra data or hyperparameters. On the knowledge-work benchmarks OfficeQA Pro and SpreadsheetBench, it reduces output tokens per episode by 57% and 53% compared with standard OPD, making the student more concise than it was before training. At the same time, it matches OPD’s accuracy on OfficeQA Pro and improves pass@1 by 4.8 points on SpreadsheetBench.

[7] SupportChain: Trace-Calibrated Aggregation of Quote-Grounded Reasoning Chains for Multi-Hop RAG with Small Readers cs.CLPDF

Zhexi Gu

TL;DR: 论文提出 SupportChain，面向多跳检索增强问答，将问题拆分为多个 hop，并把每个 hop 的答案绑定到检索段落中的引用句；随后根据每次执行自身的轨迹估计可靠性，并按答案支持度及一致执行池化可靠性合并多次执行，达到足够支持度即停止。方法无需构建图索引，可在小规模 reader 上取得优于 HippoRAG 2 等基线多跳 RAG 的效果。

Details

Motivation: 现有多跳 RAG 的强结果依赖 70B 以上大模型读取图索引，且构图需用大语言模型扫描整个语料，成本高。论文希望用较小 reader、无需索引的方式提升多跳问答的可靠性与可解释性。

Result: 在 HippoRAG 2 协议下使用 9B reader，SupportChain 在 MuSiQue 上达到 63.0 F1，超过此前使用 20B reader 的最佳结果 59.2；在相同 reader 和 embedder 下，于五个数据集上均显著优于 HippoRAG 2，最高提升 17.2 F1。按支持度合并在五个数据集中的三个上显著优于多数投票和让 reader 选择候选，其余两个持平；可靠性模型仅需 100 个带答案训练问题。

Insight: 创新点在于将多跳推理链的每步答案用检索文本引用句接地，并利用执行轨迹自校准可靠性，再以支持度和一致执行可靠性进行聚合与早停。客观上看，其价值在于用小 reader、无索引和少量训练数据实现可解释且可验证的多跳 RAG，并提供了优于简单投票的链级聚合机制。

Abstract: Strong results in multi-hop retrieval-augmented question answering come from graph indexes read by models of 70B parameters or more, and building such an index calls a large language model over the whole corpus. We present SupportChain, which splits a question into hops, binds each hop’s answer to a sentence quoted from a retrieved passage, estimates how reliable each execution is from its own trace, and merges several executions by the support of their answers, the pooled reliability of the executions that agree, stopping once support is high enough. With a 9B reader under the HippoRAG2 protocol, SupportChain reaches 63.0 F1 on MuSiQue, above the best earlier result of 59.2, which used a 20B reader. With the same reader and embedder, it is significantly better than HippoRAG2 on all five datasets, by up to 17.2 F1, and it builds no index. Merging by support is significantly better than majority voting, and than letting the reader choose among the candidates, on three of the five datasets and level with both on the other two. The reliability model needs only 100 answered training questions.

[8] From Reward Engineering to Data-Centric Reinforcement Learning for Effective Agentic Visual Tool Use cs.CL | cs.AIPDF

Jin Cui, Xinyue Long, Jiepeng Zhou, Boran Zhao, Pengju Ren

TL;DR: 论文研究多模态大模型在推理中学习何时调用外部视觉工具的问题，指出依赖工具调用相关奖励的强化学习会扭曲任务目标并导致退化调用行为，提出AOVO数据中心化框架，通过感知归因和策略自适应数据采样识别可由视觉观察纠正的失败问题，并在仅优化最终答案正确性的条件下学习有效工具使用。

Details

Motivation: 现有工具使用强化学习常用调用条件奖励鼓励有益调用，但这种奖励工程可能偏离任务目标并引发退化调用；关键不只是识别难题，而是识别哪些失败源于缺失视觉证据、能通过工具观察纠正。

Result: 在多种视觉感知与多模态推理基准上，AOVO相较有竞争力的工具使用MLLM取得一致提升；摘要称因果分析进一步验证了数据中心化视角对学习有效视觉工具使用的有效性，但未给出具体数值。

Insight: 创新点在于用反事实探测识别观察敏感问题，并用PADS按类别观察效应动态调整训练分布，避免工具特定奖励；客观看，将工具使用学习从奖励工程转向数据分布与失败归因是较有借鉴意义的方向。

Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) increasingly use external visual tools to acquire evidence during reasoning, yet learning when to invoke these tools remains challenging. Existing tool-use reinforcement learning (RL) methods often rely on call-contingent rewards to encourage beneficial tool use, but such reward engineering can distort the task objective and lead to degenerate calling behaviors. We argue that effective tool-use learning requires identifying not merely which questions are difficult, but which failures are attributable to missing visual evidence and can therefore be corrected through tool observations. We propose AOVO, a data-centric framework that enables MLLMs to learn effective tool use through perception attribution and policy-adaptive data sampling (PADS), without introducing tool-specific rewards. It counterfactually probes the model’s reasoning states to identify observation-sensitive questions, distinguishing them from reasoning-dominated ones. PADS then periodically estimates category-level observation effects from recent policy rollouts and dynamically reallocates the training distribution toward questions where visual observations provide informative learning signals, while optimizing solely for final-answer correctness. Experiments across diverse visual perception and multimodal reasoning benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over competitive tool-use MLLMs, with causal analysis further validating the data-centric perspective for learning effective visual tool use.

Abstract: The rapid proliferation of Large Language Model (LLM) research makes it increasingly difficult to distinguish incremental refinements from true paradigm shifts. This review evaluates 22 of the most influential publications spanning nearly three decades (1997-2026), organized through a causal, chronologically anchored taxonomy centered on the author’s birth year (1999). Beginning “before 1999” with how recurrent neural networks (RNNs) forgot earlier context (much like forgetting Chapter 1 by the time a reader reaches Chapter 9), we trace how Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks introduced a “bouncer” mechanism of forget, input, and output gates to selectively preserve long-term memory. We then examine how Word2Vec turned language into vector mathematics (king - male + female ~ queen), why sequential RNNs hit a parallelization wall, and how the Transformer’s all-to-all attention weights launched the modern LLM era alongside a quadratic bottleneck. Next, we analyze why scaling parameters alone leaves capacity under-trained unless data scales equally (Chinchilla), how Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) left alignment superficial, and how that gap compounded into adversarial jailbreaks and single-direction refusal subspaces (J-space), where instructing a model not to think of a restricted concept surfaces it much like the human “red ball” paradox. Finally, we synthesize the current state of AI (2024-2026), encompassing recursive model collapse, autonomous reasoning-model jailbreak agents, machine-speed agentic intrusions, and closed-loop recursive self-improvement (AIDE^2).

Abstract: Trajectory metrics promise information beyond final-answer accuracy, but no one has measured what a process score adds once an evaluation knows the outcome and the cost. We build that comparison: a sealed consequence needing an artifact neither agent nor judge ever sees, an operational baseline of terminal status and cost, and judge scale and evidence access as experimental factors. Four judges from 4B to 14B, one reasoning before scoring, add nothing an interval separates from zero; a Qwen3 32B judge on identical trajectories adds +0.050 AUC (95% CI [+0.020, +0.081]) and survives a refitting bootstrap ([+0.013, +0.095]). What the judge is shown moves it further: disclosing the terminal verdict inflates its standalone discrimination by +0.103, while reference disclosure and tool-output redaction move it by nothing an interval separates from zero. Abstract: Answering questions over long multimodal documents requires locating relevant evidence across pages containing text, tables, and figures. When the document exceeds the model’s context window, selective retrieval becomes necessary. Abstract: Multimodal knowledge graphs (MMKGs) store entities with photos and names and link them by facts. MMKG methods predict links between known entity IDs, and image retrievers, from CLIP to MLLM embedders, return entities that look like a query photo or match its description. We call this knowledge graph relational image retrieval (KRIR): given a photo and a natural-language relation, retrieve the related MMKG entity, which rarely resembles the photo, whether the depicted entity is in the graph (known) or not (unseen). We build three benchmarks from YAGO, Wikidata and in-the-wild OVEN photos. The task hides two hops: recognising which graph entity is shown, and recalling what it is connected to. GraphSeer bridges them inside one multimodal LLM: it links the photo to the graph, reads the facts of the best match, and retrieves with the hidden state at which the model is about to say the answer. An unseen entity has no facts of its own, but every candidate answer does, so a listwise verifier reads the other end of the graph: it re-ranks the top candidates by their facts and photos in one forward pass, and the facts matter far more than the photos. With Qwen3.5-27B, GraphSeer improves MRR on known entities by 24.2-70.0% over an MLLM embedder fine-tuned on the same data with the same budget. Abstract: Advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) have enabled a wide range of applications. However, their ability to simulate human-like behavior and reasoning remains unclear. We propose and evaluate PsyCoT for subjective NLP tasks, including emotion analysis, emotion intensity prediction, stress analysis, and depression severity identification. Our evaluation covers four levels of classification complexity: binary, multiclass, multi-label, and ordinal scaling, spanning 11 languages. We assess the performance of five state-of-the-art LLMs across these selected subjective NLP tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that PsyCoT prompt variants improve the standard chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting across the evaluated tasks. Across all evaluated tasks, PsyCoT yields F1 score gains ranging from 0.5% to 28.1%, depending on the model, task, and language configuration.

Abstract: Violence in films and streaming media remains a concern for audience protection and creates substantial workload for manual content classification. Our cross-domain experiments reveal performance degradation under different recording conditions, while our movie case studies demonstrate the framework’s potential to retrieve potentially violent scenes for further review. Abstract: Conditional image enhancement requires spatially varying corrections, yet fixed-depth models allocate similar computational budgets regardless of where additional refinement is needed. The revised features are processed by the shared decoder to recompute velocity, establishing feedback between transformation dynamics and internal representations. An actor-critic policy controls regional updates and further revisions to balance enhancement quality and computational cost. The learned policy reduces average decoder evaluations to 4.42 and 3.45, respectively, lowering per-slice latency from 97.00 to 51.82 ms and from 97.12 to 41.95 ms, with PSNR reductions of only 0.20 and 0.06 dB.

Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) in expert domains face a trade-off between agentic tool use, which externalizes expertise behind brittle multi-turn runtimes, and end-to-end specialization, which internalizes expertise only implicitly at task-level granularity. For training, Med-OPD performs multi-teacher on-policy distillation with token-level dual-factor teacher routing conditioned on both the image and the active capability tag, strictly generalizing per-prompt teacher routing. Abstract: Query-based 4D reconstruction models such as D4RT encode a video once into a global scene representation and obtain outputs by decoding independent point queries. In this work, we analyze the inference cost of D4RT and show that a large part of it is redundant. In particular, we find that the later decoder blocks attend to a small set of tokens shared by all queries. Based on these findings, we propose FastD4RT, a training-free framework that accelerates D4RT. By exploiting the smoothness of the outputs over time and across pixels, FastD4RT encodes and decodes only at sparse anchors and recovers the remaining outputs via interpolation. It decodes the remaining queries against a shared token set selected once per segment. We further characterize the errors introduced by both components. Abstract: Test-time adaptation (TTA) updates a model using unlabeled test data to help it handle distribution shifts. However, prior work has found that image corruption causes a vision-language model (VLM) to produce more similar features for different images, a phenomenon known as feature compression. Under compression, entropy minimization, the most common TTA objective, can cause the model to favor a few classes and perform worse than before adaptation. In this paper, we first analyze why entropy minimization fails for VLMs. We then propose CAMA, a new test-time adaptation objective that maximizes batch mutual information to encourage confident predictions for individual images while maintaining diverse predictions across the batch. CAMA also estimates a reference class distribution early in the test stream and aligns each batch’s average prediction with this reference during adaptation. We prove that feature compression biases the predictions and that entropy minimization amplifies this bias into collapse, whereas CAMA is guaranteed to preserve every class. Across standard corruption benchmarks, we observe collapse on nearly every VLM backbone evaluated. CAMA prevents collapse in every observed case and, in turn, achieves the best accuracy on every backbone. Quantitative and qualitative analyses confirm that CAMA reverses the feature compression behind the collapse, and ablations show that each of its components contributes.

Abstract: The rapid advancement of AI-generated content (AIGC) video generation and editing technologies has raised growing societal concerns about the authenticity and reliability of digital videos. Existing video detection methods primarily exploit temporal inconsistencies through holistic frame-level representations, whereas manipulation localization methods focus on artifacts within individual spatial regions. However, holistic representations may obscure localized artifacts through global feature aggregation, while region-centric approaches may overlook disagreements between individual regions and their surrounding spatiotemporal context. To address these limitations, we propose VIdeo Contextual Agreement (VICA), a unified framework that masks individual video regions and leverages a frozen V-JEPA model to predict their representations from the surrounding spatiotemporal context. Complementary masking ensures complete regional coverage, while context-conditioned predictions establish references for assessing regional agreement with the broader video context. By comparing predicted and observed representations, VICA derives spatial residuals that characterize intra-frame discrepancies and bidirectional temporal residuals that capture inconsistencies across preceding and subsequent frames. These residuals characterize contextual disagreements, providing a shared forensic representation for both tasks and shifting the focus from identifying isolated manipulation artifacts to assessing regional agreement with expectations inferred from the broader video context. Extensive experiments demonstrate that VICA achieves state-of-the-art performance on both tasks across multiple benchmarks, with strong generalization to unseen video generators and editing methods.

Abstract: A correct answer to a scientific-figure question can conceal an incorrect account of the experiment. Conditioned on both streams, our video diffusion model autoregressively reconstructs long sequences from a single temporal map. Photometric constraints and finetuning on self-generated rollouts reduce accumulated drift. At the hardware level, our approach requires only a minimal light-modulation mechanism on the lens of an event camera. We build this setup and collect a dataset comprising temporal-mapping events, motion events and synchronised ground-truth RGB frames. Experiments on a public benchmark and on our collected EvDual dataset demonstrate that EvDualDiff outperforms existing event-to-video reconstruction methods in fidelity, perceptual quality and video-level realism. Abstract: Asking a vision-language model (VLM) to think step by step often makes it worse at spatial questions, even though the image stays in context. Studying 15 open VLMs (2B-38B) and six frontier closed models, we rule out token count, turn format, and visual forgetting in open models and trace the failure through three stages. First, writing re-weights visual cues, weakening a “lower is closer” shortcut in all 13 open models tested but also discarding valid cues, which produces false relations. Second, the written text takes over. With the model’s own conclusion-removed rationale held fixed, swapping in an opposite-depth image moves the answer by 2-9 points on rendered twins (vs. up to 77 for direct answers) and by 3.0-3.4 points on average on natural photographs (vs. 20.5-69.6). This drives a coarse-to-fine evidence selection process: a coarse retrieval selects and scores all views, a diversity-aware selector reduces redundancy, and a reranking stage helps shortlist views by target visibility or answerability. The resulting evidence is optionally grounded for queries that benefit from explicit localization, and a self-verification step helps refine the final response, especially for open-ended cases. Abstract: Autoregressive Large Vision-Language Models solve multimodal reasoning tasks by retaining hundreds or thousands of visual tokens, allowing every generated token to attend to the visual tokens at any time during the generation process. Using long-form visual reasoning benchmarks and multiple model scales, we first analyze the attention dynamics across generation time and transformer depth. We identify a temporal and depth-wise structure in the use of visual information. Visual attention peaks during the initial generation steps and then rapidly declines as attention shifts toward previously generated reasoning tokens. Across depth, visual influence is concentrated in intermediate layers and becomes very weak in the final layers. We further verify these observations with causal intervention that removes all visual tokens across generation time and model depth. These interventions confirm that visual-token dependence in multimodal reasoning is neither temporally persistent nor uniformly distributed across transformer depth. Thus, retaining the complete visual context at every layer and decoding step may be unnecessary. Our experiments demonstrate that we can remove up to 59% of tokens from the full input prompt across generation time and 11% across all transformer layers, while incurring only a very small performance drop. Abstract: The rapid proliferation of multimodal social media content has made fake news detection a pressing challenge for the vision-language community. Most existing approaches rely on coarse global similarity between text and images, which overlooks subtle, uneven cross-modal inconsistencies – such as sentiment-scene mismatches, object-level manipulations, or semantic dissonance between visual and textual cues. Moreover, these models treat all inconsistencies as equally informative, ignoring domain-specific variation in how such conflicts manifest, which limits both generalization and interpretability. To address these challenges, we propose DMIL, a dual-branch multiple instance learning framework that formulates multimodal fake news detection as a weakly supervised learning problem. Each news article is treated as a bag of visual and textual instances processed through two complementary branches: an embedding-space branch that aggregates global semantics via expert-guided modality fusion, and an instance-space branch that models cross-modal inconsistencies across local-to-global granularities. A retrieval-augmented, domain-adaptive router further contextualizes inconsistencies using retrieved domain exemplars and dynamically fuses multi-level cues. Extensive experiments on public misinformation benchmarks demonstrate that DMIL achieves competitive state-of-the-art performance and demonstrates strong discriminative capability against fake news across different domains.

A current-conditioned bottleneck then learns a compact latent that captures future information relative to the present scene. This latent is predicted from the current policy context and initial Action Expert features, without access to future observations or the spatial teacher. Abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based RGB-thermal (RGB-T) remote sensing provides complementary visual and thermal information for pedestrian perception under complex aerial observation conditions. To address this limitation, we introduce a Modality Quality-Guided Collaborative Optimization Detector (MQCODet), which extends modality quality from a fusion prior to a localization supervision cue. Specifically, we propose a Dynamic Calibration and Region-Aware Fusion (DCRF) module that progressively refines cross-modal spatial alignment and performs region-aware fusion to generate reliable multi-scale features and a scene-level modality quality prior. We further design an Efficient Contextual Interaction (ECI) encoder to enhance multi-scale feature interaction while preserving fine-grained spatial details. Moreover, we propose a Modality-Aware Adaptive (MAA) loss that incorporates the modality prior and object scale to adaptively balance spatial consistency and geometric similarity for localization supervision. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MQCODet surpasses state-of-the-art methods on two UAV-based RGB-T tiny pedestrian detection benchmarks while achieving real-time inference on the edge platform.

Abstract: Executable code can preserve a world’s structural layout, yet video renderers frequently alter the appearance of previously visited places once they leave the camera view. Abstract: Unified 3D understanding and generation require compact sequences preserving spatial structure. Dense grids yield long sequences, while serialization can separate spatial neighbors. After Morton serialization, a shared LLM reads geometry for captioning and predicts tokens that decode into meshes for text-conditioned generation. With fixed geometry, architecture, and band width in voxels, sparse encoder cost grows approximately quadratically with resolution. 3D-BPE reduces mean complete LLM sequence length by 45.4 percent, including coordinates, text, and control tokens. Abstract: We present XShot, a framework for cross-shot video object insertion, which adds objects to a shot by watching another shot of the same scene. Video productions show a scene through many shots, and objects added to one shot must appear consistently in the others. Most video editors take the appearance of new objects from reference images and their location from a text prompt, a mask or an edited keyframe, leaving this consistency to the user. XShot reads both from a reference video of another shot, which need not be aligned with the target, and needs no mask, box or camera pose. We build on a video Diffusion Transformer and formulate the task as in-context generation over the reference video, a few images of the objects and the target video. A geometry-aware cross-shot attention estimates the epipolar geometry between the two shots from the model’s own correspondences and uses it to guide where the target reads the reference and the exemplars. We train XShot with an erase-and-restore data engine: objects are erased from one shot of a film or a multi-camera recording and restored from another shot of the scene. Experiments show that XShot places objects more accurately and renders them more faithfully than open-source and commercial video editors, while leaving the rest of the shot intact.

These errors quantify agreement with reference QSMs, not accuracy against destructively measured woody volume. Ablation results show that joint volume supervision is particularly important for volume control. Abstract: Visual agents navigate whole-slide images through magnified observations associated with claimed locations. However, a visually plausible observation does not necessarily originate from its claimed location, particularly across magnifications and in regions with similar tissue structures. We formulate cross-magnification provenance verification (CMPV) to evaluate whether visual evidence supports a claimed spatial association, recover the source when possible, and abstain when evidence is insufficient. We introduce PyraFault, a benchmark of 3.06 million coordinate-supervised examples from 2,200 cases across five TCGA cohorts, covering within-context substitutions, absent-source faults, and geometric perturbations. We further propose ZoomTrace, a claim-independent verifier that estimates the observation’s source before evaluating its agreement with the claimed location. It combines physical-scale alignment, visual retrieval, geometric refinement, and reliability estimation using spatially disjoint competing matches. On 503,320 test examples, ZoomTrace achieves 0.969 AUPRC and 0.987 AUROC, compared with 0.789 and 0.903 for Efficient LoFTR. Further evaluations reveal trade-offs in reliability estimation and limitations in vision-language models, cross-dataset retrieval, and calibration. Integrating ZoomTrace into visual agent tool paths reduces exposure to corrupted observations and silent failures, while downstream accuracy improvements depend on the agent and verification threshold.

Motivation: 现有手部姿态估计方法大多假设手部关节结构完整，当部分运动学结构持续缺失时容易产生不稳定或不合理预测，导致性能下降甚至系统失败。论文旨在利用部分观测在结构不完整情况下实现鲁棒且拓扑一致的手姿态估计。

Result: 在NYU/IncNYU及MSRA外部验证上，InsHaPE在结构不完整场景中提升了鲁棒性，同时在完整手上保持有竞争力的性能；系统级评估还表明其能改善依赖固定拓扑手表示的下游应用鲁棒性。摘要未给出具体数值或明确SOTA结论。

Abstract: Hand pose estimation aims to recover the spatial configuration of hand joints from visual observations and serves as a fundamental perception module for downstream systems that rely on complete and topologically consistent hand representations. Most existing methods are developed under the assumption of fully articulated hand structures and tend to produce unstable or implausible predictions when parts of the kinematic structure are persistently absent, resulting in degraded performance or even system failure despite available partial observations. To study this challenge, we construct IncNYU, a physiologically constrained benchmark that simulates structural incompleteness through morphological modification of complete hand models and retains reference locations for both intact and synthetically removed regions. Based on this benchmark, we propose InsHaPE, an Inclusive Hand Pose Estimation framework designed to remain robust under structural incompleteness while preserving performance on standard, fully articulated hands. Built on hierarchical kinematic modeling, InsHaPE introduces two complementary components. First, a topology-aware distillation strategy transfers joint-level and relational priors from fully articulated hand representations, providing anatomically consistent initialization under missing structures. Second, a progressive kinematic reasoning module performs structured inference along the kinematic chain, enabling complete and anatomically consistent pose estimation under severe structural variations. Extensive experiments on NYU/IncNYU, together with external validation on MSRA, demonstrate that InsHaPE improves robustness under structural incompleteness while maintaining competitive performance on complete hands. System-level evaluations further show that InsHaPE improves robustness for downstream applications that require fixed-topology hand pose representations.

Abstract: Chest CT reports repeatedly assess the same anatomical regions for findings and their attributes, such as whether a lung nodule is present and where it is located. These assessments suggest learning to answer visual questions directly, rather than coupling perception to open-ended text generation. Yet current CT report generation models largely follow generic vision-language modeling, which may miss subtle abnormalities when training data are limited. We therefore formulate report generation as a set of visual question-answering decisions coordinated by a large language model (LLM) agent. This decouples visual perception from reasoning and report writing: perception can be learned as a discriminative, non-generative task, while the LLM focuses on reasoning over patient context and posing relevant visual queries. We introduce Rad-VL-JEPA, which unifies report retrieval, finding recognition, and fine-grained attribute characterization through vision-language joint-embedding prediction. Building on this perception module, an agent trained with reinforcement learning (RL) acquires patient-specific visual evidence, while a separate editor incorporates the evidence into the final report, further separating evidence acquisition from report realization. Experiments show that Rad-VL-JEPA achieves strong performance on fine-grained CT understanding tasks with lower amortized per-query inference time than a generative VLM baseline trained with the same CT encoder and VQA data. The resulting reporting system outperforms strong VLM-based and agentic baselines.

Duy Tran Thanh

TL;DR: 论文提出 SpatialDuet，一种面向小型视觉语言模型的空间智能系统。它不训练单一模型覆盖所有空间任务，而是将数据驱动的度量专家与带 3D 几何编码器的几何专家组合起来，并用贝叶斯任务路由器按问题类型动态融合两者答案。度量专家还引入采样、最小贝叶斯风险解码和分类型度量校准等免训练模块。

Details

Motivation: 具身助手和可穿戴设备需要 3D 空间推理，但硬件受限只能使用小型 VLM；不同小型空间 VLM 在不同空间任务上各有优势，因此与其训练一个全能模型，不如按任务类型路由到最擅长的专家。

Insight: 创新点在于用贝叶斯任务路由器按问题类型估计专家更优概率并融合答案，数值答案在对数空间池化、选择题在选项分布上池化；同时以免训练方式增强度量专家，实现冻结模型间的互补协作而非统一训练。

Abstract: Embodied assistants and wearable devices need 3D spatial reasoning, and their limited hardware restricts them to small vision-language models (VLMs). Small spatial VLMs acquire different abilities from their training: a model trained on large spatial question sets estimates object and room sizes well, whereas a model with a 3D geometry encoder is better at relative directions and absolute distances. Instead of training a single model for all spatial tasks, as published methods do, we build one system that uses each frozen model for the tasks it handles best. We propose SpatialDuet, which pairs a metric expert with a geometry expert under a Bayesian task router. The metric expert is a data-driven spatial VLM run with three training-free modules: training-aligned sampling, metric-aware minimum Bayes risk decoding and per-type metric calibration. The geometry expert is a VLM with a 3D geometry encoder. For each question type, the router estimates from labelled development questions how likely each expert is to be better, and pools their answers with that probability as weight, in log space for numeric answers and over the option distributions for multiple-choice answers. Extensive experiments on four spatial benchmarks covering video and single images validate SpatialDuet; it outperforms the best published small VLMs by 3.17% on VSI-Bench and, excluding a model trained on CV-Bench-style data, by 1.44% on CV-Bench, without training any model weight.

TL;DR: 论文提出 loopxDINO，用迭代潜在推理替代传统密集视觉预测中堆叠深层前馈解码器的方式。模型冻结 DINOv2-Base 主干并缓存 Key-Value，使用紧凑的权重共享循环交叉注意力解码器在多次迭代中更新查询，并通过多种稳定化机制和中间掩码反馈提升训练与边界预测。在 Pascal VOC 2012 语义分割上，以更少参数取得更高 mIoU 和 Boundary IoU，并具备更好的遮挡鲁棒性和自适应计算能力。

Motivation: 传统密集视觉预测依赖堆叠 6-16 层 Transformer 解码器扩展容量，带来反向传播激活内存开销、非共享权重的高片外内存带宽需求，以及无法按图像空间复杂度自适应分配计算的问题。论文希望用迭代潜在推理替代物理层深，在降低参数和内存成本的同时保持或提升密集预测性能。

Abstract: Standard dense visual prediction architectures scale representation capacity by stacking deep feedforward decoders (6-16 transformer layers with 50M-200M parameters). This explicit layer stacking brings substantial activation memory overhead during backpropagation, requires high off-chip memory bandwidth for non-tied weights, and uses static computational allocation that cannot adapt to spatial image complexity. It has two decoupled components: (1) a frozen DINOv2-Base backbone extracting spatial features in one forward pass and caching static Key-Value representations in GPU memory; (2) a compact weight-tied Looped Cross-Attention Decoder (7.96M core, 14.85M total trainable parameters) that recurrently updates queries across T iterations. It outperforms 6-layer DINO-Trans6L (54.06M params) by +1.09% mIoU and +7.41% Boundary IoU with 72.5% fewer parameters. Compared to 4-layer DINO-FCN4L probe (2.43M params, 83.82% mIoU), loopxDINO improves boundary delineation by +6.43% bIoU and occlusion resilience by +6.76% mIoU (60% patch masking). With Adaptive Computation Time (ACT), it reaches 87.3 FPS and retains 29.64% mIoU under 60% occlusion (+5.83% over DINO-Trans6L). Source code, pre-trained weights and evaluation suites are open-sourced under Apache 2.0 at https://github.com/loopxDINO/loopxDINO

Abstract: Physical counterfactual video editing turns a source video and a language-specified physical edit at a given execution frame into a counterfactual video that shows how the scene would evolve after the edit. Existing evaluations with counterfactual target videos mainly cover object removal or specific rigid-body motions, although real scenes also involve elastic deformation, fluid flow, and interactions among rigid bodies, elastic solids, and fluids. We introduce PhyCoVE, a benchmark of 533 cases on 110 source videos that covers rigid, elastic, and fluid dynamics in five interaction patterns, with edits that remove an object, change a physical quantity, or insert a new object. For the simulated cases, a language model proposes scene designs, coding agents build them with solvers suited to each material and physically based rendering and then simulate each edit from the source scene state, and humans check every stage. For the real cases, we record continuously from one camera position before and after each edit. We also propose counterfactual fidelity, a metric that applies across materials and their interactions and measures how much of the physical change from the source video to the target video a generated video reproduces. We evaluate seven open-source and commercial video editing models and find that counterfactual fidelity ranks them nearly as human preference does, but even the best model reproduces only about one seventh of the physical change. The models change how a scene looks but rarely how it evolves, whereas a physical edit requires understanding the dynamics that it changes. Physical counterfactual video editing thus remains far from solved, and PhyCoVE provides a foundation for developing and evaluating methods for it.

Abstract: Standard 3D point cloud language models typically rely on pretrained point encoders to extract 3D features and project them into representations processable by large language models (LLMs). However, these encoders are often originally optimized for pre-defined tasks, resulting in a representation bottleneck that may lead to a substantial mismatch with downstream 3D understanding. Moreover, existing models largely follow a single pass closed-book generation, limiting their ability to actively inspect task-relevant 3D regions or retrieve necessary external knowledge. In this work, we present PointTool, an encoder-free and tool-augmented framework for 3D reasoning. PointTool introduces Alignment-Free Patch Tokenization (AFPT) to locally aggregate raw point clouds while preserving fine-grained geometric structure, and Decoupled Point-Text LoRA (DPL) to facilitate global aggregation and 3D knowledge internalization within a frozen LLM. Building upon these designs, Program-Supervised Tool Reasoning (PSTR) enables the model to explicitly operate on raw 3D data and external resources through executable tools, supporting interactive 3D reasoning grounded in spatial evidence. We further introduce PointCloud-TR, a benchmark comprising 13K 3D objects, 39.8K questions, and 35.6K tool trajectories to facilitate training and evaluation of complex 3D reasoning. Abstract: We present PartPO, a reinforcement learning method for generating structured shape programs from 3D point clouds. Existing shape-to-program models are trained with supervised learning on procedurally generated data and generalize poorly to more diverse shapes, while reinforcement learning from execution feedback assigns a single scalar reward to a long program that builds many parts, making credit assignment difficult. Abstract: Cross-view UAV geo-localization involves three design choices: how to represent the UAV observation, how to represent the geo-referenced map, and how to infer pose from their interaction. Abstract: Geometry-aware rotary positional encodings, such as RayRoPE, help attention reason about the 3D spatial relationships between tokens and the query camera. For dynamic scenes with temporally separated input views, this mismatch places the same moving object at a different position in each input frame, so it can be rendered at an inaccurate position. While temporal encodings inform attention when a token was observed, they do not resolve where its content should be at the query time. Abstract: Clinical computed tomography (CT) interpretation inherently requires progressive visual exploration, where radiologists navigate from whole scans to individual slices and regions of interest and interact with external tools when necessary. Abstract: Visual token pruning can reduce the inference cost of vision language models, but its effectiveness depends on preserving complementary visual information under a limited token budget. Abstract: Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) enables contactless physiological monitoring from facial videos, but facial motion, particularly mouth and jaw movements during cognitive and communicative tasks, can severely degrade signal reconstruction. Building on this finding, we introduce SKIA-Net, a compact spatiotemporal architecture that combines raw facial frames, statically masked representations, and temporal motion differences to reconstruct blood volume pulse (BVP) waveforms. The full model achieves a Pearson correlation of 0.7522 and a heart-rate MAE of 3.73 bpm on UBFC-rPPG, outperforming single-stream variants. Ablation studies show that the static mask provides complementary information to raw appearance and that static anatomical priors outperform the tested dynamic optical-flow-based masking strategy. Abstract: Prompt learning provides a parameter-efficient way to adapt pretrained vision–language models through text and visual prompts, but noisy labels prevalent in real-world data inevitably bias prompt updates and thereby undermine adaptation effectiveness. Prior work on robust prompt learning focuses on suppressing unreliable updates under noisy supervision. However, suitable prompt allocations vary across tasks and are unknown a priori, rendering brute-force candidate training computationally prohibitive. Using a small sample of images and generated pseudo-labels as shared supervision, GPrompt performs an initialization probe to extract paired text and visual loss gradients, and characterizes the geometry of their trace-normalized Gram matrices through both concentration within each modality and overlap between modalities. GPrompt then derives a closed-form allocation, and projects it onto feasible prompt counts under the exact parameter budget, enabling task-specific selection without training candidate configurations. Experiments across eleven datasets show that GPrompt outperforms the strongest baseline by up to 7.75% while selecting configurations close to the best allocation identified through exhaustive training. Abstract: Deep learning has shown promise for estimating human pose with multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar through walls. These pose features then guide diffusion in the MIMO-VAE latent space, and the VAE decoder reconstructs echoes from the generated latents. Abstract: Vision-language models have become a new kind of describer, writing about almost anything people see, and their descriptions now shape how cultures are known by people and by other models. Model descriptions give each object many faces, each typical of its culture and almost none the object itself.

Abstract: Current MLLM methods largely focus on whether models attend to the right visual regions, implicitly treating spatial attention map as the primary key of effective visual perception. We show that this view is incomplete: across paired NC and CE medical images, MLLMs often exhibit similar attention patterns despite producing contrasting answers, while controlled bidirectional interventions induce substantially larger prediction changes on visual values than attention weights. Abstract: World models support robotic manipulation by predicting how the scene evolves under a planned action. We introduce ClothCast, a world model that applies this prior to the cloth’s points and learns the residual motion. ClothCast takes one RGB-D observation, the camera pose, the robot’s own model and the planned gripper trajectories, with no cloth mesh or material parameters. It lifts the observation to a layered point set that includes hypothesized occluded layers, carries the points with a blended rigid prior derived from the gripper poses, and predicts the residual motion with a video-diffusion point-flow model. Over entire 4- to 11-second episodes at 10 Hz, the moved points are rendered into depth, from which a geometry-conditioned completion model synthesizes RGB; after release, a hand-designed settling step replaces the learned motion. We further release ClothCastBench, 10,000 simulated dual-arm cloth-manipulation episodes with the ground-truth cloth mesh, including occluded layers, at every frame. On 492 held-out episodes, ClothCast achieves 2.5x lower sequence-averaged visible-surface Chamfer distance than Flex-π, the strongest baseline in geometry (14.0 mm vs. 35.6 mm), and 3.7 dB higher cloth-region PSNR than Cosmos-Predict2.5, the strongest baseline in cloth PSNR. Abstract: Unsupervised spectral super-resolution aims to recover spectral information from RGB images without paired hyperspectral data. The representation module constructs a continuous spatial-spectral representation via shared spectral and local spatial Gaussian primitives, exploiting the low-rank spectral structure of hyperspectral images. The rendering module utilizes the spectral response function (SRF) to apply integral projection to the continuous representation, blending it to generate an RGB image. Consistency between the rendered and observed RGB images provides training supervision. Our main contribution is a Gaussian splatting framework that integrates structured continuous spatial-spectral representation with imaging response-based rendering, enabling unsupervised spectral reconstruction. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art methods.

Abstract: Distribution matching distillation (DMD) enables fast video generation by distilling a multi-step teacher into a few-step student. However, DMD-based methods often suffer from unnatural motion and costly training. We trace these limitations to the DMD gradient, which jointly optimizes appearance, layout, and motion without distinguishing their learning dynamics. Its static component, which carries appearance and layout, has a much higher signal-to-noise ratio than its motion component. As a result, per-frame quality converges within a few hundred iterations, whereas motion lags far behind. Beyond being noisy, the gradient also lacks two signals. (1) Video VAEs encode several frames into one latent frame (four in Wan2.1), and the gradient provides little guidance for spreading motion over these frames, causing periodic stutter. (2) DMD does not constrain the final sampling step to preserve the layout set by earlier steps, so objects merge and drift once the video moves. Abstract: Aligning text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models with human preferences typically relies on large-scale pairwise annotations, which are expensive to obtain and provide only sparse supervision. Motivated by this observation, we propose PrefLens, a framework that recovers local preference neighborhoods from sparse human feedback. Specifically, PrefLens generates controlled perceptual variations around preferred images that largely retain semantic identity and selects compact sets of informative neighbors in a reward-defined preference space induced by pretrained reward models. Motivation: 旋转、平移或缩放照片中的物体需要揭示未见表面、保持可见外观并更新光影，而重建的3D资产纹理不完美会与照片冲突，标准配对训练未明确教编辑器何时信任照片、何时信任3D状态。

Result: 在OBJect和SpatialEdit-Bench上展示了强空间编辑性能和内容保持能力，受控消融实验表明方法改进了源选择并在采样时持续响应条件。

Insight: 创新点在于用反事实构造训练信号：通过隐藏表面重绘、隐藏几何重渲染光影、可见表面纹理替换构建受控冲突来监督源选择，并用状态侧/照片侧孪生构造有向潜在扰动训练校正；仅训练时操作，无需架构修改或额外推理步骤，为条件生成中的源信任问题提供了可借鉴的训练范式。

Abstract: Rotating, translating, or rescaling an object in a photograph requires revealing unseen surfaces, preserving visible appearance, and updating shadows and reflections. Reconstructed 3D assets, rendered at the target pose as a 3D state, provide explicit geometric guidance, but their imperfect textures may conflict with the photograph, while standard paired training does not explicitly teach the editor which source to trust. To address this, we propose counterfactual state supervision, which constructs controlled photo–state conflicts through hidden-surface repainting, hidden geometry with re-rendered shadows and reflections, and visible-surface texture replacement. This teaches the editor to follow the 3D state for unseen content while preserving photograph-visible appearance. However, learning this distinction does not ensure that it is maintained during sampling. We therefore introduce symmetric counterfactual correction, which uses state-side and photo-side twins, which share the photograph and the state respectively, to construct directed latent perturbations toward condition-inconsistent targets and train recovery toward the target specified by the current condition. Both strategies operate only during training, requiring no architectural changes or additional inference steps. Experiments on OBJect and SpatialEdit-Bench demonstrate strong spatial editing performance and content preservation, while controlled ablations show improved source selection and sustained responsiveness to conditioning during sampling.

TL;DR: 论文提出 SCRA-CLIP，一种面向零样本异常检测的球面上下文表示适配框架，联合增强异常感知的文本语义和上下文敏感的视觉表示。方法包含球面原型条件提示 SPCP 和上下文偏差引导视觉适配 CGVA，用于提升细粒度异常检测与定位中的跨模态匹配能力。

Motivation: 现有视觉语言模型虽支持零样本异常检测，但对多样异常模式及其空间上下文的建模不足，导致细粒度异常检测仍具挑战。论文旨在同时改进异常相关文本表示和上下文敏感视觉表示。

Insight: 创新点在于用 von Mises-Fisher 混合建模正常/异常 patch 特征的方向分布，并将状态特定原型注入文本提示；同时通过多尺度邻域上下文偏差和自适应门控精炼视觉 patch 表示。客观看，其可借鉴之处是联合分布感知的语义建模与上下文敏感的视觉适配，以增强细粒度跨模态异常匹配。

Abstract: Recent advances in vision-language models have facilitated zero-shot anomaly detection (ZSAD) through transferable visual-semantic representations. However, detecting fine-grained anomalies remains challenging due to inadequate modeling of diverse anomaly patterns and their spatial context. To address these challenges, we propose SCRA-CLIP, a Spherical-Contextual Representation Adaptation framework that jointly enhances anomaly-aware textual semantics and context-sensitive visual representations. Specifically, we introduce Spherical Prototype-Conditioned Prompting (SPCP), which employs von Mises–Fisher mixtures to model the directional distributions of normal and abnormal patch features. These state-specific prototypes are incorporated into textual contexts to guide the learning of more discriminative textual representations. Furthermore, we develop Context-Deviation Guided Visual Adaptation (CGVA), which captures local feature deviations relative to multi-scale neighborhood contexts and refines patch representations through adaptive gating. By integrating distribution-aware semantic modeling with context-sensitive visual adaptation, SCRA-CLIP facilitates more discriminative cross-modal matching for fine-grained anomaly detection and localization. Extensive experiments on 11 industrial and medical benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and generalization capability of SCRA-CLIP across diverse unseen categories and domains. The code will be publicly available upon publication.

Peng Chen, Chao Huang, Yangyang Liu, Maodong Wu, Jinyi Xu

TL;DR: 论文提出EVAD，一个面向工业异常检测的证据引导视觉搜索框架。它先进行全局视觉评估定位潜在异常区域，再借助MCTS引导的探索策略，通过语义细化和空间扩展逐步获取并验证细粒度视觉证据，最终支持MLLM做出更可靠的异常判断。

Details

Motivation: 现有基于多模态大模型的工业异常检测方法多依赖全局观察，难以主动获取和验证细微异常所需的细粒度视觉证据，导致异常识别与推理不够可靠。

Result: 在多个工业异常检测任务的广泛实验中，EVAD在大多数评估设置下达到SOTA性能，验证了主动证据探索对细粒度异常理解与推理的有效性。

Insight: 创新点在于将“先检查再决策”的证据引导视觉搜索引入MLLM异常检测，结合全局评估、MCTS探索、语义细化与空间扩展来逐步收集和整合诊断性证据；客观上，其价值在于用主动多尺度证据获取与验证增强细粒度异常推理的可靠性。

Abstract: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable potential for industrial anomaly detection and understanding. However, reliably identifying subtle anomalies remains challenging, as existing approaches often struggle to acquire and verify fine-grained visual evidence beyond global observations. To address this challenge, we propose EVAD, an evidence-guided visual search framework that enables MLLMs to actively seek and examine diagnostically informative visual evidence for reliable anomaly reasoning. Specifically, EVAD begins with a global visual assessment to identify potentially anomalous regions for further inspection. Building upon this observation, we introduce a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)-guided exploration strategy that progressively acquires visual evidence through two complementary operations: semantic refinement for fine-grained inspection and spatial expansion for contextual verification. The acquired evidence is subsequently evaluated and integrated to support more informed and reliable anomaly decisions. Extensive experiments across multiple industrial anomaly detection tasks demonstrate that EVAD achieves state-of-the-art performance in most evaluated settings, highlighting the effectiveness of active evidence exploration for fine-grained anomaly understanding and reasoning. The code will be publicly available upon publication.

Details

Motivation: 动态相机下从单目视频恢复全局一致 3D 人体运动仍具挑战；SLAM 与 HMR 虽互补，但直接结合易产生朝向不一致和轨迹漂移，因此需要一种更稳定的耦合方式。

Result: 在 EMDB-2 上，使用 ViPE 达到 154.0 mm W-MPJPE100 的 SOTA；使用 masked DROID-SLAM 为 189.8 mm，优于 TRAM 的 222.4 mm；同一 HMR 骨干下，相比 GVHMR 的 276.5 mm 降低 44.3%，相比 GVHMR+HTD-Refine 的 192.4 mm 降低 20.0%。

Insight: 创新点在于以共享重力对齐参考系解耦并耦合 SLAM 与 HMR，允许重力独立于 HMR 骨干估计，并通过 YAOO 与 GATO 联合校正朝向和轨迹。客观看，其价值在于训练免费、即插即用，并利用人体度量尺度与 2D 重投影缓解直接融合导致的朝向不一致和轨迹漂移。

Abstract: Recovering globally consistent 3D human motion from monocular videos remains challenging under dynamic camera motion. Although SLAM and human mesh recovery (HMR) provide complementary camera and body estimates, directly combining them often leads to inconsistent orientations and accumulated trajectory drift. We present GravHMR, a training-free, plug-and-play framework that couples SLAM and HMR through a shared gravity-aligned reference. By allowing gravity to be estimated independently of the HMR backbone, GravHMR accommodates world-grounded HMR models with or without explicit gravity-view representations. Specifically, Yaw-Aware Orientation Optimization (YAOO) resolves heading inconsistencies by correcting body and velocity orientations about the shared gravity axis. Conditioned on these corrected orientations, Gravity-Aware Trajectory Optimization (GATO) anchors root trajectories in the metric SLAM world by jointly leveraging 2D reprojection, the metric scale implicit in the human body, and the body’s own motion. On EMDB-2, GravHMR achieves state-of-the-art performance with 154.0 mm W-MPJPE100 using ViPE and 189.8 mm using masked DROID-SLAM, outperforming TRAM (222.4 mm) under the same masked DROID-SLAM camera estimates. It further reduces W-MPJPE100 by 44.3% over GVHMR (276.5 mm) and by 20.0% over GVHMR + HTD-Refine (192.4 mm) with the same HMR backbone.

Yiyu Li, Fei Wei, Yong Wang, Zaiquan Yang, Gerhard Petrus Hancke

TL;DR: 论文针对DMD蒸馏实时自回归视频生成中reverse-KL目标mode-seeking导致样本多样性、时序动态下降和颜色过饱和的问题，提出Mass Forcing概率质量感知框架，将on-policy DMD监督从整段视频细化到单个状态。方法从共享学生前缀分支多个续写，估计教师-学生密度比并重加权DMD更新，同时用重加权参考分布进行跨rollout监督。

Details

Motivation: DMD的reverse-KL目标会让学生条件视频分布坍缩到少数模式，现有通过学生初始化提升覆盖的方法效果短暂，训练中动态视频比例仍快速下降，说明mode-seeking目标本身是退化主因。

Insight: 创新点在于将DMD的mode collapse问题转化为状态级概率质量失配，利用on-policy分支估计教师-学生密度比，对欠表示rollout重加权，并通过跨rollout对齐提供更细粒度监督。客观上看，该思路把整段视频监督细化到状态级概率质量校正，在不增加推理成本下兼顾多样性与时序动态。

Abstract: Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) has emerged as a promising paradigm for real-time video synthesis, distilling pretrained diffusion models into few-step autoregressive generators. However, its reverse-KL objective is mode-seeking and can collapse the student’s conditional video distribution onto a narrow subset of modes, leading to reduced sample diversity, diminished temporal dynamics, and color oversaturation. Existing methods mitigate this issue mainly via coverage-oriented student initialization, but we observe that such coverage is transient: across three initializations, the fraction of dynamic videos drops sharply during subsequent DMD training, indicating that the mode-seeking objective, not the initialization, drives this degradation. We propose Mass Forcing, a probability-mass-aware framework that moves on-policy DMD supervision from whole videos to individual states. Each update branches several continuations from a shared student-generated prefix, making the student’s probability mass at that state measurable against the teacher. First, Mass Forcing estimates relative teacher-to-student density ratios among these continuations through latent-space score integration and uses them to rebalance conditional DMD updates, amplifying rollouts underrepresented relative to the teacher. Second, since mismatched mode probabilities do not necessarily induce strong local score corrections, it aligns generated rollout sets with a reweighted reference distribution defined by the same mass estimates, providing cross-rollout supervision. Experiments on MovieGen and VBench show that Mass Forcing improves video fidelity and sustains temporal dynamics throughout training, achieving the highest Total scores among compared methods and a Dynamic Degree of 83% after 1,000 generator updates, versus 12-32% for the baselines, with no additional inference-time overhead.

[189] SuperFine3D: Efficient Global-Local Recursive Refinement for Extremely Detailed 3D Geometry Generation cs.CVPDF

Lihan Li, Junwei Zhou, Yu-wing Tai

TL;DR: 论文提出SuperFine3D，一个通过全局-局部递归细化从图像高效生成极细节3D几何的框架。它学习共享细化算子并在粗到细表示上递归复用，从而在无需目标分辨率配对监督的情况下合成超出训练分辨率的精细几何。方法引入空间单元注意力和空间锚定跨尺度引导，在保证结构一致性的同时降低高分辨率计算开销。

Details

Motivation: 高分辨率图像包含丰富细节，需要精细几何结构才能忠实重建3D；但现有方法从图像生成极细节3D几何时面临计算资源和训练数据需求过大的问题，高分辨率几何生成困难。

Insight: 创新点包括：从粗到细配对表示学习共享细化算子并递归复用至更高分辨率；空间单元注意力将高分辨率交互限制在局部空间邻域并保持相邻单元有界通信；空间锚定跨尺度引导利用全局上下文粗几何指导局部细节合成；几何感知训练目标在引入细粒度表面细节时保持几何结构稳定。

Abstract: High-resolution images contain rich visual details that require fine geometric structures for faithful 3D reconstruction. However, generating extremely detailed 3D geometry from images requires substantial computational resources and training data, making high-resolution geometry generation challenging for existing state-of-the-art models. In this paper, we present SuperFine3D, an efficient framework for generating extremely detailed 3D geometry through global-local recursive refinement. SuperFine3D learns a shared refinement operator from paired coarse-to-fine representations and recursively reuses it to progressively synthesize finer geometry beyond the training resolutions, without requiring additional paired supervision at target resolutions. To make recursive refinement computationally efficient, we introduce spatial-cell attention, which restricts high-resolution interactions to local spatial neighborhoods while maintaining bounded communication across neighboring cells. We further propose spatially anchored cross-scale guidance, which leverages globally contextualized coarse geometry to guide local detail synthesis and preserve structural consistency. In addition, geometry-aware training objectives encourage the refinement process to preserve stable geometric structures while introducing fine-grained surface details. Experiments demonstrate that SuperFine3D generates geometry at a $4096^3$ decoder-grid resolution, corresponding to a sparse $256^3$ latent lattice, using a shared refinement operator trained only on $512^3$–$1024^3$ representations. Compared with a full-attention recursive baseline, SuperFine3D achieves a $9.4\times$ speedup in end-to-end inference and reduces peak GPU memory usage by $23.0%$, while improving cross-scale structural consistency and producing cleaner surfaces with finer geometric details.

Xinrui Gong, Yao Rong, Chuangtao Chen, Daniel Ochs, Ulf Schlichtmann

TL;DR: 论文提出 DeclareViT，用于高效 Vision Transformer 的提前退出推理。它通过为每个出口设置专用 query，以单向交叉注意力读取中间特征，从而将早期分类与主干特征细化解耦，同时冻结主干和最终分类器，仅训练出口分支。

Details

Motivation: ViT 推理计算成本高，现有 early-exit 方法将早期分类与共享主干耦合，中间表示需同时服务早期分类和后续特征细化，联合训练易产生梯度方向冲突。

Abstract: Vision Transformers achieve remarkable recognition performance but incur substantial computational cost during inference, limiting their use in latency- and compute-constrained deployment scenarios. Early-exit inference offers a promising solution by allowing easy samples to terminate at intermediate layers. However, existing approaches typically couple early classification with the shared backbone, requiring intermediate representations to support both early classification and subsequent feature refinement. Under joint training, the corresponding optimization objectives jointly update shared backbone parameters, which can lead to conflicting gradient directions. Motivated by this observation, we introduce DeclareViT, a framework that decouples early classification from feature refinement. Each exit uses a dedicated query to read intermediate features through one-way cross-attention without modifying the backbone token stream. The query branches are optimized for early classification while the backbone and final classifier remain frozen. Across ViT, DeiT, and Swin on CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1K, and Food-101, DeclareViT consistently establishes a state-of-the-art accuracy-efficiency trade-off: It achieves 1.58 times to 2.57 times multiply-accumulate (MAC)-based speed-up with only a 0.39-1.91 percentage-point accuracy drop. Wall-clock measurements on CPU and GPU further demonstrate practical inference acceleration. Code is available at https://github.com/TUDa-HWAI/DeclareViT.

[191] Ref2Light: From One Image to Interactive Glasses-Free 3D Characters cs.CV | cs.AIPDF

Hanzhong Zhang, Haoyang Wang, Siyang Song

Motivation: 现有 2D 动画和 3D 重建管线难以同时满足光场显示所需的双目视差一致性、实时姿态关节控制、细粒度表情控制和快速角色切换，且通常依赖逐角色重建或优化。

Abstract: Animating character illustrations on light-field displays demands coherent binocular parallax, real-time pose articulation, and fine-grained expression control. However, existing 2D animation and 3D reconstruction pipelines cannot combine these with rapid character switching. We present Ref2Light, a feed-forward framework that maps a single A-pose illustration and continuous pose and expression controls to display-native light-field animation, without per-character 3D reconstruction, rigging, or test-time optimization. Our key insight is to decompose light-field synthesis into static identity, view-dependent parallax, and control-driven articulation. A shared encoder caches multi-scale identity features once per character for rapid switching. A conditional decoder then synthesizes ordered angular anchors from these features via backward texture transport and direct color synthesis. A global-local control scheme deforms the anchors with head-body controls and uses the updated correspondence fields to track facial regions across views for masked local facial refinement. Finally, calibrated differentiable subpixel interlacing converts the anchors into the native panel raster, enabling end-to-end native supervision without rendering all views at full resolution. On held-out VRoid identities, Ref2Light reduces head-body LPIPS by 20.1%-55.6% over 2D and 3D baselines and lowers non-target change MAE in mouth closure by 95.6%-96.5% versus monolithic decoding, while running at 34.0-40.1 FPS for 1440x2560 native rasters on a consumer GPU. Code and demo are in the Supplementary Material.

Chaoyang Zhang, Shaohao Rui, Xiaofeng Mao, Yuanxun Xu, Haoyuan Xia

TL;DR: 论文提出 HandiVid，一个面向手部驱动的第一视角交互视频生成的高质量数据集，包含约 20 万个经过筛选和标注的第一视角交互视频片段。作者构建统一数据处理流程，融合公开数据集、在线视频和合成视频，并通过视频质量评估、手部检测过滤和基于 VLM 的多阶段交互验证筛选高质量样本，同时提供手部渲染、相机轨迹和交互描述。

Abstract: Hand-driven egocentric interactive video generation aims to generate dynamic scenes with realistic interaction responses conditioned on hand movements and camera motion. However, existing egocentric video datasets struggle to provide scene diversity, meaningful hand-object interactions, and reliable motion annotations simultaneously. To address these limitations, we introduce HandiVid, a high-quality dataset comprising 200K curated and annotated egocentric interaction video clips for hand-driven interactive video generation. We develop a unified data processing pipeline that integrates public datasets, online videos and synthetic videos. Through video quality assessment, hand detection filtering, and multi-stage interaction validation using vision-language models (VLMs), we select high-quality video clips with meaningful hand-object interactions. Since 3D hand reconstruction relies on initial hand detections, we integrate SAM 3 into the hand detection pipeline to reduce missed detections and improve the completeness of 3D hand annotations. Each video clip is provided with high-quality hand renderings, camera trajectories, and interaction descriptions. Comprehensive dataset analysis and downstream video generation experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of HandiVid in terms of data diversity, annotation quality, and controllable video generation.

Abstract: This paper presents a novel framework, Unified Diffusion modeling and Registration (UniDR), which learns to generate arbitrary anatomical deformations from images with preserved topology. Existing approaches often model the generative process separately from registration-based deformation estimation; hence making them prone to propagated errors from the registration stage. To address this limitation, we propose a unified paradigm based on a conditional diffusion model over deformation fields that are jointly optimized from the registration process. A principled registration-guided score-matching objective function is then introduced to align the diffusion process with the deformation distribution induced by registration. As a result, our UniDR establishes an explicit connection between generation and registration: the diffusion model enables exploration of the space of plausible anatomical deformations, whereas registration provides structured supervision for learning transformations consistent with observed images. Once trained, UniDR is able to sample diverse, anatomically plausible transformations conditioned on any single input image. We evaluate UniDR across multiple real-world applications and demonstrate its effectiveness in generating high-fidelity image samples compared to the state-of-the-art. Additionally, we demonstrate that these generated samples improve performance in downstream medical image analysis and vision tasks.

Abstract: Animal re-identification (Re-ID) must distinguish individuals across species and capture conditions. We introduce ApexID, a hierarchical SphereFace2-based loss that integrates global identity discrimination with balanced animal-category supervision. Using 132,533 images curated from 19 public datasets, we evaluate three model families and four objectives on four external datasets with observation-aware retrieval protocols. ApexID achieves a dataset-averaged Rank-1 accuracy of 64.89% with ConvNeXt-Small and an mAP of 32.54% with MIEW-ID, outperforming their pretrained reference models. On elephants, a category absent from animal Re-ID training, our ConvNeXt-Small variant achieves the highest retrieval performance among the fourteen evaluated configurations. Scores vary by backbone and dataset, and open-set evaluation reveals remaining discovery challenges. These findings support hierarchical category-identity learning to improve transfer to unseen datasets and species.

Abstract: Reasoning distillation offers a promising approach to transfer temporal reasoning capabilities of powerful Video-LLMs to open-source student models. However, teacher and student Video-LLMs may construct different temporal observations from the same video due to the adoption of distinct video sampling pipelines. A reasoning trajectory valid under the teacher’s observations may rely on evidence inaccessible to the student and thus cannot be directly executed based on the student’s observations. We formalize this as a conditional target mismatch, thereby revealing the Reasoning Acquisition-Execution Gap. To bridge this gap, we propose an acquisition-to-execution framework that first distills teacher trajectories into a student reasoning prior and then further optimizes the execution capability of this prior across multiple observations. We further introduce Execution-Aware Reference Regularization, which retains the existing prior when it is executable under current observations, while allowing a greater degree of adaptive adjustment when it is not. Experiments across multiple Video-LLM backbones and six video reasoning benchmarks show that explicitly optimizing observation-conditioned execution consistently outperforms supervised distillation and standard RL-based optimization, with gains extending to held-out out-of-domain benchmarks.

Abstract: A zero-shot vision-language classifier is highly sensitive to the class names it receives. Even when images remain unchanged, replacing familiar labels with synonyms, abbreviations, or ontology terms can significantly alter predictions. We investigate this \emph{vocabulary shift} using a leakage-free evaluation protocol across Tiny ImageNet, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-A, and ImageNetV2. With CLIP ViT-B/16, alternative class names reduce top-1 accuracy by $14.8$–$17.6$ percentage points. To address this issue, we propose \emph{image-grounded concept linking}, a training-free method that maps class names to visual concepts and uses a reliability gate to improve predictions. The method outperforms a template ensemble across all four datasets, achieving a pooled gain of $1.8$ points. We further evaluate five vision-language backbones across four datasets. Our method improves performance in $16$ of $20$ backbone–dataset combinations, with no significantly negative results. It also reduces pooled negative log-likelihood across all five backbones. Stronger text linking and transductive refinement provide no consistent improvements, suggesting that accurate visual class-name linking remains the main challenge. A second CLIP ViT-B/16 seed confirms the improvement on ImageNetV2, but not on ImageNet-A.
